decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) an abrupt multi-axis jump near the end of the first window (indices 539–541), and (2) a coherent drop in N and E near the end of the second window (indices 658–661), both warranting closer inspection for potential physical motion or instrumental offset.

regions.observation: A sharp, multi-sample jump in all three axes (N/E/U) occurs around index 539–541, with N increasing from ~12 to ~17, E dropping from ~-6 to ~-2, and U rising from ~12.8 to ~19.5; the change is abrupt and sustained, suggesting a possible permanent offset or rapid motion event.

After a period of relatively stable high-amplitude motion (N~28–30, E~6–8, U~1–3), a distinct drop in N and E occurs around index 658–661 (N from ~29.5 to ~27.6, E from ~7.8 to ~6.1), possibly indicating a return or opposing shift; the U component shows less coherence but remains within prior range.
